card_name: 1968 Topps Complete Set Basic With Wax Pack #2
condition_note: One of the finest sets with a #2 ranking on the PSA Set Registry.
special_note: Includes 271 cards at PSA 10 GEM MINT level.
description_block:
The design of the 1968 Topps series has always been a topic of debate for vintage collectors, many lauding it for its straightforward appearance that often allows the cards to present at a higher level than the technical grade, while others criticize the collection for its "lack of pizazz" in comparison with more colorful issues of the previous years. But one this they all seem to agree on is that the lineup of superstars, along with the Johnny Bench and Nolan Ryan rookie cards, is as good as any collection distributed in the 1960s. The featured set is one of the finest we've ever seen, boasting a #2 ranking on the PSA Set Registry with an incredible 9.905 GPA. A set of this elite caliber is going to be loaded with PSA 10 GEM MINT examples, and this one offers 271, or over 45%, of cards at PSA's top level, including #8 ERA Leaders, 11 Strikeout Leaders, 86 Stargell, 145 Drysdale, 215 Bunning, 310 Aparicio, 363 Carew, 364 Morgan, 371 Oliva, and 372 Brock. Every other card is graded PSA 9 MINT except for #177 Ryan rookie card PSA 8. The included wax pack is also graded PSA 8. This collection is being offered as a complete set as well as each card being offered individually, with the final method of sale based on whichever total (the set versus the sum of the individual lots) is higher. For a complete breakdown of grades and populations, please visit our website for a link to the PSA Set Registry.

description_block: Chosen 6th overall in the 1957 NFL draft, Jim Brown led the league with 972 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns, earning MVP honors. From there, he just kept getting better, snagging another MVP award the next season with a league-leading 1,527 yards and 17 touchdowns. In fact, he led the league in rushing in 8 of his 9 NFL seasons, retiring at the age of 29 after winning his third MVP award, and still stands as #1 all-time in rushing yards per game at 104.3. The 1958 Topps Jim Brown rookie card is a staple in any world-class collection, and very few possess the perimeter sharpness of the featured PSA 8 example. Though mildly shifted toward the right, the card possesses above-grade corner sharpness as clearly evidenced on the bright red reverse, which yields far less chipping than most at this grade level. If you haven't yet added a stunning NM/MT example of arguably the gridiron's premier pasteboard, this is your opportunity to score one of the most important examples in the sports card trading hobby.

description_block: With so much hoopla surrounding the legendary T206 Honus Wagner card, even the most savvy of collectors can overlook "The Flying Dutchman" in many of the more obscure issues, with the number of known examples coming in far lower than the T206 card. The featured example from Wagner (batting variation) comes from the 1910 E105 Mello Mint series, and with a population of just 28 for SGC and PSA combined, the card is far more scarce than the T206 without having to dole out millions of dollars to acquire one. The featured example is the only SGC 2.5 on record, with just one graded higher at SGC 3. The corners show consistent rounding that aligns with the grade, and the centering favors the left edge, but the image of Wagner and the surrounding red backdrop are as fresh as they were over a century ago. Equally impressive is the retained whiteness surrounding the image, having repelled any discoloration that is often found on gum and candy issues from this era. The slightly toned reverse houses nostalgic, spearmint-green print that advertises Mello Mint gum. This is a truly remarkable example that rarely becomes available, so don't miss the opportunity to land this beauty!

description_block: Of all the truly iconic sports cards that have spanned the history of baseball, it can be argued that the first one chronologically is the 1887 N28 Allen & Ginter issue of Adrian C. "Cap" Anson. Considered the first bona fide superstar in baseball history, Anson's 3,435 career hits (#7 all-time), .334 lifetime batting average, eight RBI titles, and 4 batting crowns made him the Ted Williams of his day ... or was Ted Williams the Cap Anson of his day? The card has been assessed as altered by PSA, but the overall appearance is truly remarkable. Centered lightly toward the top, the mid to upper-grade endpoints and an impressively sharp image of Anson will have you scratching your head, wondering how a card almost 140 years old can look this amazing. Some missing paper on the back would have kept any numerical grade to a minimum, but for sheer eye appeal, it would be hard to find a better value!

Robinson (PSA 7.5) and #123 Koufax (PSA 6). This collection is being offered as a complete set as well as each card being offered individually, with the final method of sale based on whichever total (the set versus the sum of the individual lots) is higher. special_note: Iconic debut card of Hall of Famer Frank Robinson.
description_block: The 1957 Topps series is loaded with important rookie cards, but none are more iconic than the debut card of Hall of Famer Frank Robinson. A Most Valuable Player award winner in both leagues, "The Judge" is often overlooked among the likes of such legends as Mays, Mantle, and Clemente, but Frank Robinson's achievements are truly Cooperstown worthy, finishing his career with 586 homers and a .294 batting average. Here's Robinson on his debut card, having successfully taken Rookie of the Year honors with 38 homers and a .290 batting average at just 20 years old. Four stunningly sharp corners of true MINT quality set the stage for the seemingly unyielding boundaries, while the central image is simply incredible, rich in bold red color that transcends typical exemplars, even those sharing the spotlight at the PSA 9 level. Add in the virtually perfect centering and overwhelming red and blue pigment practically jumping off the slate gray canvas on the reverse, and you've got a world-class example of a key 1950s rookie card, tops in its field with no GEM MINT examples on record.

description_block: Like his rival across the river, named Mickey Mantle, Hall of Famer Willie Mays didn't make the big splash as a rookie that many historians expected. Though "The Say Hey Kid" was named the National League rookie of the year, his 20 home runs, 68 RBI, and .274 batting average in 1951 were considered underwhelming for such an explosive talent. Having missed most of 1952 and all of 1953 to military service, when this 1953 Topps card was distributed, most fans outside of New York were saying, "Who's Willie Mays?" Mays returned in 1954 to capture the National League batting title, stealing bases like Ty Cobb and slamming homers at a rate that had some thinking he might dare catch the great Babe Ruth. The featured example offers eye appeal closer to the NM/MT mark, near perfectly framed with a glorious central image of the young Mays, flanked by corners and edges that are NM to NM+. The reverse is equally superior, prompting Mike Baker Authenticated (MBA) to assess a Silver Diamond award for extraordinary eye appeal.

description_block: Babe Ruth may stand forever as the baseball juggernaut that started the Yankees dynasty, but it was teammate Lou Gehrig who displayed the consistency and perseverance in taking the torch from "The Babe" and building a tradition that made "The Bronx Bombers" the most storied franchise in all of sports history. And while Gehrig's 1933 and 1934 Goudey cards stand as the gold standard for vintage collectors, it's "The Iron Horse's" far more scarce 1932 U. S. Caramels issue that world-class hobbyists actively seek to advance their collections. Graded PSA 6 EX/MT, the featured card is mildly toward the left edge with a well-focused image of the iconic Yankee first baseman. The four corners retain a sharpness not often encountered for an EX/MT assessment, and compare well with examples at the NM level. The fire engine red surrounds the central image, bringing attention to the subject, while the reverse is a bold, well-inked bio set forth in jet black, set against a creamy white stock and devoid of any pitfalls. A tremendous card offered in strong EX/MT condition that we feel borders on NM.

description_block:
The 1951 Bowman baseball series stands as one of the most important issues ever to represent the hobby of card collecting. Originally designed to be a 252-card series, the headliners of the collection were to be Ted Williams, Yogi Berra, Roy Campanella, Bob Feller, Warren Spahn, Pee Wee Reese, and Duke Snider, with the rookie card of Hall of Famer Whitey Ford to stand as the key debut pasteboard of the set. Bowman likely thought that after "The Chairman of the Board" posted a 9-1 record and 2.81 ERA with 7 complete games over 12 starts in his 1950 Yankees debut, placing him as card #1 of the series would've had the same effect as, say, card #1 of the Upper Deck series with Ken Griffey Jr. Ironically, Ford didn't even play in 1951 as he had started his two-year stint of military service. But as fate would have it, a couple of other budding superstars were coming to "The Big Apple," and    Bowman made the last-minute decision during the production's run to expand the set by 72 cards,  including the Mickey Mantle and Willie Mays debut cards within the new high-number series and taking the collection from what would have been ordinary to legendary in the eyes of vintage collectors. The featured assemblage is one of the best on record, ranked #6 overall on the PSA Set Registry with an 8.167 GPA, with the Mantle and Mays cards needed for completion. Every card in the set is, at minimum, graded PSA 8, with the following that are rated even higher: PSA 9 (41 cards) - #14, 19, 42, 48, 49, 63, 73, 74, 75, 77, 84, 94, 111, 128, 141, 149, 157, 160, 175, 180, 191, 192, 193, 202, 203, 205, 207, 212, 214, 220, 222, 231, 232 Fox RC, 236, 240, 241, 277, 280, 294, 309, and 322. PSA 8.5 NM/MT+ (27 cards) - #51, 60, 66, 67, 68, 92, 98, 103, 105, 123, 139, 147, 158, 167, 168, 169, 184, 201, 206, 209, 213, 228, 230, 245, 247, 291, and 321. For a complete breakdown of the grade and population of each card, please click on the link for the PSA Set Registry.

description_block: The 1951 Bowman Willie Mays rookie card is one of the most iconic issues since the very first trading card was introduced to the American public nearly a full century before "The Say Hey Kid" made his way to the big leagues. As it stands, the featured PSA 5 example of Willie Mays's rookie card is one of, if not, the most eye-pleasing specimen in the hobby for the grade. It's debatable as to which amazing attribute is more impressive on this card; the incredible corners that appear more like NM to NM+, or the extremely accurate centering that most cards actually graded NM to NM+ cannot match. If not for two mild roller lines, one of which ably blends into the backdrop, the featured card would likely be at least one grade higher, possibly more. The reverse offers substantial confirmation, centered to near perfection with a clean canvas enhanced by bold and sharp print. You can't beat this specimen at the PSA 5 level!

special_note: Ranked #6 on the PSA Set Registry Current Finest list with a 7.480 GPA.
description_block:
The 1955 baseball season marked the final independent baseball card set for Bowman. The full color player (and umpire) photographs were presented with an appealing, mahogany-trimmed TV set design that would serve as a template for various future sets like the classic 1966 Topps football and hockey sets. At this point, Bowman was losing the battle to Topps for exclusive rights to star players; hence, no issue of Stan Musial, Ted Williams, Jackie Robinson, or Duke Snider, nor do the "big three" rookies Sandy Koufax, Roberto Clemente, and Harmon Killebrew appear in the 1955 Bowman set. However, Bowman did have Mickey Mantle in their stable, and the set remains one of the most sought-after issues of the 50s in high-grade due to the sensitive nature of the borders. The master set includes 6 error cards that were corrected and reissued: #48 Milt Bolling (Frank on back), 101 D. Johnson (wrong photo), 132 Kuenn (spelled Kueen on back), 157 E. Johnson (wrong photo), 195 Palica (no trade reference), and 204 Frank Bolling (Milt on back). Presented is one of the most spectacular 1955 Bowman master sets in existence, ranked #6 on the PSA Set Registry Current Finest list with a 7.480 GPA. Other than one card graded PSA 8.5 (#287), the entire set is in the PSA 7 to PSA 8 range with 193 cards graded PSA 8 (including #23 Kaline, 37 Reese, and 134 Feller). One card is graded PSA 7.5 (#153), and the rest of the cards are graded PSA 7, including #1 Wilhelm, 10 Rizzuto, 22 Campanella, 59 Ford, 103 Mathews, 158 Hodges, 1698 Berra, 179 Aaron, 184 Mays, 202 Mantle, and 242 Banks. This collection is being offered as a complete set as well as each card being offered individually, with the final method of sale based on whichever total (the set versus the sum of the individual lots) is higher. For a complete breakdown of grades and populations, please visit our website for a link to the PSA Set Registry.

special_note: This is the only PSA 6 EX/MT example of Ty Cobb on record, with none graded higher.
description_block: Even the most advanced Ty Cobb collectors likely have this piece unchecked on their list, as it is perhaps the rarest of all pasteboards that feature "The Georgia Peach." Originating from the 1922 WM Paterson set from Canada, a collection so scarce that only 83 examples have been graded at PSA out of the entire 50-card series, comes this PSA 6 EX/MT example of the legendary Ty Cobb. Of those 83 cards, eight of the graded pieces are of Cobb, and this is the only PSA 6 EX/MT on record, with none graded higher, the next highest being PSA 4. While Cobb rightfully won his share and everyone else's share of American League batting titles, earning 12 titles in 13 years, this one got away from him as, at 35 years old, Cobb batted .401 but lost out to MVP winner George Sisler and his amazing .420 clip. The card is truly remarkable and displays the old-world charm expected of an obscure 1920s Canadian print, displaying pedestrian font as if created on a vintage typewriter, and displaying the home of the company as "Brantford. Canada." The real-life image of Cobb is sublime as it fully captures the spirit of the hard-nosed legend, surrounded by a bright white backdrop that shows near-perfect framing. The corners and edges uphold EX/MT standards, and the reverse shows some light age but impresses nonetheless. A truly remarkable piece that few of even the most world-class of collectors can boast to owning.

description_block: Aside from his pitching achievements, he was the greatest all-around hero of the Deadball Era, a handsome, college-educated man who lifted the rowdy world of baseball to gentlemanliness. Matty was the basis, many say, for the idealized athlete Frank Merriwell, an inspiration to many authors over the years, and the motivation for an Off-Broadway play based on his life and writings. “He gripped the imagination of a country that held a hundred million people and held this grip with a firmer hold than any man of his day or time,” wrote sportswriter Grantland Rice. The featured cardboard collectible is easily one of the most popular pasteboards of the tobacco era, as well it may as well be one of the most difficult cards to find in top tier condition. Projecting a stunning image of the "Christian Gentleman" shot by Charles Conlon in 1911, the featured card offers a flawlessly focused image full of vibrancy not normally encountered. Superior presentation of a centered image is further emboldened by corners as well as edges that are the caliber of a much higher graded example. Each of the four endpoints come to exact ninety degree angles void of wear with any white that may appear along the edges being from the original cutting production of the keepsake. The colors are abundant and richly applied with an overall presentation really enchanted. The reverse is void of any disturbances and offers a nearly perfect application of red ink on the Sweet Caporal advertisement. MBA has recently graded this deadball collectible and conservatively assessed a grade of NM 7 with an addition of a silver MBA sticker denoting superior eye appeal which is the highest sticker designation they make on cards residing within their own holder. A terrific example that stands out as one of if not the finest examples of this immensely popular card that we have ever offered.

special_note: Celebrates Ohtani's achievement of joining the '50-50 club' and his potential Hall of Fame status.
description_block: While many baseball purists have found it audacious to compare Shohei Ohtani to the immortal Babe Ruth, "Shotime" is starting to turn naysayers into believers. His 2025 NLCS and World Series heroics that helped lead the Los Angeles Dodgers to a championship support the case; 6 home runs and 9 RBI over 11 games while batting .341, and also posting 19 strikeouts over 14 1/3 IP on the mound. Ohtani has proven to be dominant on both offense in defense, which hasn't been seen since "the Bambino" pulled it off early in his career before switching to a full-time outfielder. The featured card is one of the rarest of all Ohtani issues, a 2024 Topps Orange Jersey Auto card that originates as a redemption card from the exclusive "50/50" series, celebrating his achievement of becoming the first and only member to join "the 50-50 club" with 54 homers and 59 stolen bases in 2024, which led to his third league Most Valuable Player award over four years. This example sits in its original case and is numbered #12/25, and it is unknown if all 25 that have been produced have been accounted for. If you can imagine what an exclusive card like this would be in the days of Babe Ruth and what its value would be today, that could be exactly where we are headed in the future when Ohtani takes his place in Baseball's Hall of Fame.

description_block: Most vintage collectors are familiar 1958 Hires Root Beer cards for their familiar wood-paneled backdrop, even without the tab. But not many hobbyists know about the Hire's test set, which offers a more monotone look similar to the 1941 Goudey series. The image of "The Say Hey Kid" is the same, but the test series features Willie Mays in a black and white presentation with a bright orange backdrop. Examples of these surface from time to time, but this specimen is the one and only SGC 6 with none graded higher. The card displays mostly EX/MT to NM characteristics with minimal chipping along the colored edges, save for the perforated side where the tab originally was. The reverse is uncommonly clean and problem-free. One of the toughest finds on the expansive Willie Mays checklist.

He started 73 games and pitched every inning of every game; 73 complete games. In fact, he completed 97% of the 502 game starts in his career. Reasonably well centered with above-grade sharpness around the perimeter, the central image is one of the lighter examples, but it still provides a clear image of the baseball pioneer. A rare and alluring example!

Solid numbers for sure, but for the die-hard pinstripers that expected "The Commerce Comet" to take his place among Ruth, Gehrig, and DiMaggio as the next Yankees immortal, his performance left them wanting more. And more they got! The 1955 season was Mantle's breakout campaign, earning his first home run crown with 37 round-trippers while also leading the American League with 11 triples and 113 walks, and posting a .306 batting average, a precursor to his Triple Crown season in 1956. And with his absence in the 1955 Topps set, Mickey Mantle's 1955 Bowman card stands at the forefront of the Mantle library. While it's expected that the wood-grained edges and endpoints will likely expose some significant chipping, this PSA 8 example is an exception. Well-framed with a magnificent image and endpoints that expose virtually nothing, even the reverse is up to the task, a clean, problem-free canvas. Hall of Famer Brooks Robinson joins "The Hammer" on the three-card panel, as does Larry Dierker, but Aaron was the star of the piece, as he would finish the 1970 season just eight homers short of the 600 home run milestone. For Hank Aaron collectors aiming for the top spot on the PSA Palyer Registry, this specimen represents a significant step toward moving up the rankings.

Unlike rookie cards and highly popularized examples of Babe Ruth, the 1986 Fleer Michael Jordan card, even at a grade as high as this PSA 8 NM/MT example, can still find its way into many collections. The featured piece is a fine representative of the grade, typically shifted slightly to the left-to-right centering, but well-compensated with slightly above-grade corners and edges that have resisted chipping more so than most at its grade level. The reverse offers a clean canvas that is specifically well-positioned. With the price of examples like this seemingly moving upward with every offering, you really need to lock one down for your prized collection.

description_block: Even though a PSA 8.5 NM/MT+ grade for any vintage card is impressive, it always leaves us wondering if, on another day, the card would grade PSA 9 MINT. Unitas was a 9th round draft pick in the NFL draft by the Pittsburgh Steelers before ever taking a snap, deemed "not smart enough" to process the speed of NFL decision-making. The Steelers lost out on that one, but you don't need to lose out on this high-end NN/MT+ example. Outstanding centering and borderline MINT corners help support the dual images on the surface, bursting with green and orange colors required for such a lofty assessment. The reverse is, in a word, bold, with brilliantly deep black and red pigmentation pressed onto the clean slate gray canvas. With just 13 examples graded higher, this card would be a welcome addition for any collector looking to make up the standings on the PSA Set Registry leaderboard.

Bowman added Jackie Robinson to their 1948 Leaf lineup, a collection that features several important rookie cards, but none that have the societal impact of a baseball card that introduces the first black player in major league history. The featured card is perhaps the best value we've ever seen for the winning bidder, graded 4 VG/EX by Mike Baker Authentication (MBA) but offering the appearance of a card at the NM to NM/MT level. card_name: 1957 NAACP Freedom Fund Campaign Jackie Robinson
condition_note: Well-delivered image of Robinson with virtually no loss of black pigmentation at the edges.
special_note: Important role in civil rights and baseball history.
description_block: Having broken baseball's long-standing color barrier in 1947, Jackie Robinson was the logical choice to chair the NAACP's million-dollar Freedom Fund Drive in 1957, one of the organization's most pivotal events that led to the passing of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. While 1957 was the only year that Robinson chaired the drive, he remained on the board of directors for the NAACP until 1967. Other than a few surviving posters and perhaps a letter or two, there are very few examples of items from the 1957 NAACP Freedom Fund Campaign that offer the image of the legendary Jackie Robinson, but one such piece is this borderless "card" that features the Hall of Fame legend in a black and white, borderless portrait. Although technically a "folder" since the coupon on the reverse was meant to be cut or "folded over" to contain the monetary donation to the cause, the featured piece exists in scarcity, as most recipients either discarded it or used it for its intended purpose. This survivor is one of the best-known examples on record at BVG with an EX/MT 6 grade that features a well-delivered image of Robinson and virtually no loss of the black pigmentation at the borderless edges of the thin stock. This is a wonderful example of one of baseball's most important figures, once again confirming the important role that baseball has played in shaping the norms of American society and featuring Jackie Robinson as, once again, a champion of civil rights.

condition_note: Only PSA 6 example on record with none graded higher.
special_note: One of the most elusive cards in the Ty Cobb library.
description_block: While the T206 White Border series is the most celebrated tobacco issue of the early 20th century, many smaller issues that originated from confectionery companies were lightly regarded by collectors for decades. But those days are over. Presented is one of the most elusive cards in the Ty Cobb library, an E92 Croft's Candy specimen of "The Georgia Peach" that would marvel even the most advanced collector in any grade, but this PSA 6 example would be equally appropriate on display at a museum as it will be in the hands of the winning bidder. Only 12 examples of this card have been evaluated by PSA, a quantity that pales in comparison to the legendary T206 Honus Wagner card. And of those specimens known to exist, the featured card is the best of the best; the only PSA 6 example on record with none graded higher, a full two grade points ahead of the next best PSA-graded example. The vast majority of cards from this series reside in the PSA 2-PSA 4 range, displaying heavily rounded corners and faded pigmentation of what was once a bright and bold series. This Cobb card stands as a reminder of what was, displaying a fine artist's rendering of Cobb against a radiant yellow background that has retained all of its bold beauty. The corners are so surprisingly squared that even the most seasoned of vintage collectors will be impressed, likely never having seen an E92 of any subject this well-preserved, let alone the 12-time American League batting champion. The centering is quite astute for the series, as a mild to bottom centering variance is all there is to report in place of the usual wild framing that often results in grading qualifiers. Finally, the Croft's Candy reverse is boldly printed with some slight age discoloration expected of a piece that is well over a century old. If you're a collector of "The Georgia Peach" or trying to raise the status of your collection to the next level, this one-of-one gem will do it!

special_note: Important rookie card of Jackie Robinson, notable for its historical significance.
description_block: The crude 1948 Leaf Baseball set is besieged with quality-control issues from poor centering to out-of-focus images to even variations in color and shade. So when landing some of the more important cards (and it doesn't come any more important than Jackie Robinson's rookie card), you have to "pick your poison" on what you're willing to tolerate, especially in lower grades. And with this PSA 3.5 VG+ example offering mostly above-grade features, you don't have to sacrifice much. A moderate smattering of stray print is evident on the surface, but the perimeter sharpness, overall boldness of color, and astute centering all come in at a level superior to the assessment. The reverse is even more impressive, a clean slate with bold print that stacks up against copies in the EX/MT to NM range. This is a very attractive example for the rather conservative grade.

special_note: Ranked #17 on the PSA Set Registry with an impressive 7.869 GPA.
description_block:
With another year of quality card-making under their belt and the competition from Bowman long in the past, Topps once again expanded their annual collection by upping the 1959 set to a whopping 572 cards. In addition to the usual cards were the inclusion of several subsets; the 22-card All Star series, the 31-card "Rookie Stars" selection, the 10-card "Baseball Thrills" series, and the popular multi-player cards, with such memorable issues as "Fence Busters" (Aaron/Mathews), "NL Hitting Kings" (Mays/Ashburn), "Corsair Outfield Trio" (Clemente, etc.) and many others. The featured Master Set ranks #17 on the PSA Set Registry, with an impressive 7.869 GPA. Highlights include 15 cards graded PSA 9 MINT (#224, 225, 257, 318, 399, 410, 415 Mazeroski, 419, 422, 432, 434, 437, 438, 490, and 552 Stengel). There are four cards graded PSA 8.5 NM/MT+ (#53, 261, 262, and 377). The large majority of the set, 541 cards, are graded PSA 8, including #20 Snider, 30 Fox, 40 Spahn, 149 Bunning, 155 Slaughter, 163 Koufax, 180 Berra, 202 Maris, 212 Fence Busters, 260 Wynn, 270 Hodges, 317 NM Hitting Kings, 350 Banks, 352 Roberts, 360 Kaline, 387 Drysdale, 380 Aaron, 390 Cepeda, 430 Ford, 435 F. Robinson, 439 B. Robinson, 450 Mathews, 478 Clemente, 515 Killebrew, 550 Campanella, 563 Mays AS, and 564 Mantle AS. Other notable cards are: PSA 7 - #150 Musial, 514 Gibson RC, and 561 Aaron AS. PSA 6 - #50 Mays. PSA 5 - #10 Mantle. This collection is being offered as a complete set as well as each card being offered individually, with the final method of sale based on whichever total (the set versus the sum of the individual lots) is higher. For a complete breakdown of grades and populations, please visit our website for a link to the PSA Set Registry.

The brilliance of the white border is further amplified by the perfectly framed central image, displaying a wonderfully focused image of "The Commerce Comet", with plenty of bold red pigmentation as it appeared fresh out of the pack. Each of the four corners breezes by MINT standards and makes a case for PSA's top assessment. The reverse is every bit as impressive as well, an unusually gleaming white canvas with deep, clean pigments of black and salmon laid upon it, clearly and concisely laying out the iconic resume of The Mick over his then 15 years of major league service to that point. A spectacular specimen!

description_block:
The final set of their Play Ball trilogy was released in 1941, similar to their black-and-white photographed predecessor but with the fronts printed in color, often just using colorized versions of the player’s 1940 card. Trimmed down from 240 issued cards in the 1940 set, the ’41 Play Ball version contains just 72 cards and can occasionally be found in their original 12-card sheets. While small in size, the 1941 Play Ball set was big in star power, with popular issues of Mel Ott, Jimmie Foxx, Hank Greenberg, Charlie Gehringer, Ted Williams, Joe DiMaggio, and the rookie card of Pee Wee Reese, among others. For Greenberg, Williams, and DiMaggio, this would be their last largely manufactured issue before temporarily leaving baseball to serve the United States in the war effort. The offered 1941 Play Ball is complete. and completely PSA graded, rating #17 on the PSA Set Registry with a 5.57 GPA. Included are the following: PSA 8 (7 cards) - #17, 22, 25, 28, 34, 41, and 63 D. PSA 5 (15 cards) - #4, 8 Ott, 21, 27, 30, 32, 45, 46, 49, 50, 51, 59, 61, 67, and 72 Gomez. PSA 4 (9 cards) - #9, 14 T. Williams, 18 Greenberg, 29, 33, 39, 64 Doerr, 65, and 70 Dickey. special_note: Museum-quality piece, significant addition for advanced collectors.
description_block: There are dozens of issues dedicated to "The Georgia Peach", some originating from obscure candy, confectionery, and tobacco companies, in addition to the quartet of hobby icons in the T206 series. But none of those other examples show Ty Cobb in such luxurious and alluring detail as this oversized M101-2 Sporting News Supplement. Having gone unnoticed as a bench player in his first two seasons, Cobb took the starter's role in 1907 and captured batting and RBO crowns over the two years leading up to the start of the Sporting News Supplement series. This representation of 22-year-old Ty Cobb was readily available to the public in the early 20th century, but very few have survived, and only 26 submissions of this issue are on record at PSA. This is the best one in existence; the only PSA 4 on record with none graded higher, the next best example earning a PSA 3 grade, making it a significant addition for any advanced collector on the PSA Player Registry. Even with that "one-of-one" grade, you can't help but think that piece deserved even higher praise, given the EX/MT to NM level sharpness of the perimeter and the incredible image of Cobb, easily the most comprehensive delivery of the baseball legend and 12-time American League batting champion ever offered on a nationally distributed specimen. This is a museum-quality piece that will help define a world-class collection

condition_note: Rounded corners indicative of a lower grade, but presents well with deep color and decent centering.
special_note: Universally recognized as the toughest and most significant T206 card outside of 'The Big 4.'
description_block: When it comes to the T206 series, once you move past the Wagner, Plank, Doyle variation, and "Magie" cards, issues so rare they are excluded from the mainstream T206 set, the honor of "most elusive T206 issue" falls onto the Bill O'Hara "St. Louis" card. Though traded by the New York Giants to the St. Louis Cardinals during or shortly before production, the tobacco companies had already released the O'Hara card as a member of the Giants. All except Polar Bear. The company reflected the change in their tobacco issues; thus, it is the only issue that shows O'Hara as a member of the Cardinals. While the exact number of existing specimens is unknown, the "St. Louis O’Hara" is universally recognized as the toughest and most significant T206 card outside of "The Big 4." The offered specimen is graded SGC AUTHENTIC and shows rounded corners indicative of a lower grade, but presents well with deep color and decent centering. An excellent, rare specimen at an affordable price.

special_note: One of only 17 packs with a Michael Jordan rookie card graded PSA 8.
description_block: It's the dream of every advanced collector to open a pack of 1986 Fleer basketball cards and score the grand prize of the set, perhaps the grand prize of the entire baseball card hobby: a Michael Jordan rookie card. But as most who have taken the plunge find out, the odds aren't in your favor. And while there are plenty of other key rookie cards that could potentially recoup the investment and maybe even turn it into a slight gain, it's the debut piece of MJ that makes it a "boom-or-bust" endeavor. Well, there's no guesswork here as "his airness' has announced his presence for all the world to see, directly on top of this wonderful pack as verified by PSA. While the pack has been graded PSA 8, that puts no limitations on the quality of the MJ card housed just underneath, making this not only a rare item as is, but a very lucrative venture for a daring speculator. Out of almost 2,300 packs graded by PSA from the 1986 Fleer set, there are only 22 that have the popular Michael Jordan rookie card on the top of the pack. This is one of only 17 to grade a PSA 8, with only one graded higher.

description_block: An issue that somehow got overlooked for decades, advanced collectors are now starting to appreciate the beauty and significance of the sprawling M101-2 Sporting News Supplements series. Loaded with baseball legends, fewer were more popular than Christy Mathewson when this series began in 1909, having posted a 114-44 record and 1.84 ERA with two ERA titles and three strikeout crowns over the four seasons leading up to 1909. This example of Hall of Famer Christy Mathewson is the highest graded on record at PSA and the only PSA 4 specimen with none higher, the next best of the scant 19 submissions coming in a PSA 2.5. As impressive as the assessment is, it still seems like the grade is very conservative, given the deep, penetrating tone of the image and sharpness of the endpoints, a rare feat considering how thin the paper stock is. The blank reverse has stayed remarkably clean, save for a few small and inoffensive shades of discoloration. This is a truly phenomenal piece of "Big Six" that does not exist in this condition anywhere known.

condition_note: Includes three PSA 10 GEM MINT cards and numerous high-grade examples.
special_note: One of the greatest compilations of 1956 baseball cards ever assembled.
description_block:
The 1956 Topps baseball release remains one of the most persistently popular sets in cardboard keepsake history, with exploding submission numbers on record at PSA and an increasingly glaring deficiency of high-grade examples. Like its two predecessors, the 1956 cards employ both a portrait and an action picture, yet the newly conceptualized action shot consisted of a full image as opposed to just a cut-out, spawning such unforgettable images as Mickey Mantle soaring into the outfield bleachers to rob a home run, or Jackie Robinson and Willie Mays sliding in for a score, perhaps just after stealing home. Other innovations in the 1956 set include the popular and today immensely coveted team cards, several of which report multiple challenging variations that help comprise the “master set”, as well as famous "rookie" cards of League Presidents, Williams Harridge and Warren Giles, plus the first-ever Topps checklists. As if to eventually counter these novel introductions, however, the 1956 set marked the last time Topps would employ artwork (or artistically enhanced images), and it also marked the last of the great over-sized sets of the early ‘50s, a tradition going back to the groundbreaking 1952 set. Notable inclusions are Ted Williams, Jackie Robinson (his last Topps card), Mickey Mantle (his first Topps card since 1953, just in time for his 1956 Triple Crown Award), Luis Aparicio (his rookie card) and Willie Mays, Hank Aaron, Roberto Clemente, Sandy Koufax, and the coveted team cards of rival powerhouse clubs, the New York Yankees and Brooklyn Dodgers. What is offered here, with extreme pride, is one of the greatest compilations of 1956 baseball cards ever assembled, a nearly complete master set that checks in at #4 on the PSA Set Registry with an 8.466 GPA and includes three PSA 10 GEM MINT cards: #13 Face (one of 2), 34 Brewer (one of 3), and 201 Repulski (one of 2). Highlights include 192 cards graded PSA 9 MINT with #109 Slaughter, 111 Red Sox Team, 120 Ashburn, 307 Wilhelm, and Checklist 1/3. There are 23 cards graded PSA 8.5 NM/MT+, led by #33 Clemente, 183 Roberts, and 251 Yankees team. The 131 cards graded PSA 8 include #1 Harridge, 5 T. Williams, 10 Spahn, 15 Banks, 20 Kaline, 30 J. Robinson, 31 Aaron, 79 Koufax, 101 Campanella, 107 Mathews, 110 Berra, 113 Rizzuto, 130 Mays, 145 Hodges, 150 Snider, 164 Killebrew, 200 Feller, 240 Ford, 260 Reese, and 292 Aparicio. Card #!00 Orioles Team-Dated, is graded PSA 7, and four cards are graded PSA 6: #95 Braves Team-Dated, 100 Orioles Name Left, 100 Orioles Name Centered, and 135 Mantle. This collection is being offered as a complete set as well as each card being offered individually, with the final method of sale based on whichever total (the set versus the sum of the individual lots) is higher. For a complete breakdown of grades and populations, please visit our website for a link to the PSA Set Registry.

description_block: When the 1968 Topps rookie card featuring Hall of Famer Nolan Ryan was released, collectors overwhelmingly considered it to be the Jerry Koosman card. After all, Koosman was a highly touted hurler who ended up recording 222 victories and amassing 2,556 strikeouts during his 19-year career. He even came within a whisker of beating out Johnny Bench for National League Rookie of the Year honors. However, the other guy, this Ryan character, racked up 324 victories and an astounding 5,714 strikeouts, along with a record seven no-hitters, so it's pretty safe to say this is the Nolan Ryan rookie card now. The featured example offers razor-sharp NM/MT images of both pitching aces, with NM/MT corners and a noteworthy lack of stray pink print rings in the susceptible purple circle. A slightly more accurate centering placement would probably have warranted a higher grade.

As an inaugural issue, it's loaded with "rookie" cards of players that had already established themselves, and no player needed to "prove their worth" more than the first black player to break the long-standing color barrier. Had Robinson failed and washed out of the league, this specimen may have been the pariah of the set, but Jackie's Rookie of the Year status and stolen base crown made this card one of the most highly prized in the series, amplified further when he won MVP honors in 1949. The featured example has sidestepped the large majority of quality-control issues that relegate them to the lower grades, delivering a sharp and well-centered piece that still feels a bit conservative at the PSA 6.5 level. Even the usual smattering of stray print that gets caught in the yellow pigmentation is at a bare minimum. Few examples that carry this assessment have avoided all of the potential significant pitfalls of the issue like this one has, leading Mike Bake Authenticated (MBA) to deliver a Silver Diamond assessment for exceptional eye appeal.

description_block: Graded NM 7 by MBA with an MBA Silver sticker for superior eye appeal. The featured example is a recently graded gem that stands out as the finest example we have ever offered in a NM holder from any grading organization. Adopting an aggressive, take-no-prisoners style of play which mirrored his fiery temperament and abrasive personality, Cobb dominated the game in the batter’s box and on the base paths. At the plate, the 6’1", 175-pound left-handed swinger often gripped the bat with his hands several inches apart, but usually brought them back together during his swing. A powerful hitter, Cobb led the league in slugging percentage eight times, and paced the circuit in doubles three times and triples four times. Yet he was also a scientific hitter who liked to beat out bunts and infield grounders for base hits. After 1920, Cobb became a passionate defender of the Deadball Era-style of play, derisively mocking the “swing crazy” batters of the modern game who had neglected the inside strategies mastered by the Georgia Peach. The offered collectible is a stunning convergence of four strong upper end NM+ to NM/MT endpoints that project an overall grade minimally two grades in advance of the opined assessment. The centering is nearly perfect and easily meets qualification of a more stringent qualification. The color is a rich vibrant hued red with a nearly perfect deep well focused image of the great batsman that easily is atop the finest examples we have encountered. MBA has conservatively graded the prideful pasteboard NM 7 crowning the grade with a silver MBA sticker for the aforementioned superior eye appeal. (which is there highest assessment of sticker given on their own holder) A card that presents vastly superior in presentation to nearly every example extant of grade and grading organization.
